fear.name: Despair
fear.hint: The Despair pool of the GM.

forceDiceLook.name: One dice look for the table
forceDiceLook.hint: Every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice in the look of one full Gamemaster, fixed the first time the game runs with it on, with no special effects but those a Gamemaster marks as global, and a change of their own goes back to it. Another full Gamemaster's own look stays theirs and changes nothing for the table beyond the effects they mark as global. Each keeps their own display and performance settings. Switching this off gives nobody their old look back.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player roll is whispered to that player and the GMs, and a GM's roll to the GMs. Nobody sees anyone else's dice. The one roll everybody sees is the GM panel's Public roll (game.drpg.publicRoll) - a vote's tie, Monokuma's lottery.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Another player's sheet opens redacted: name, portrait, Health, Sanity and what they are holding. Statistics, Hope, actions, inventory and Truth Bullets are hidden. Each player still owns their own sheet in full.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: How many times one room can be searched in a single time of day.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot touch the dice, the statistic, advantage, experiences or the bonus - those come from the action, a Hope Call or the GM. Spending an experience is the Experience Hope Call. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides other characters unless they stand in the same room. Walls and vision get most of the way there; this closes the gaps left by doorways, archways and maps built without walls. GMs see everything.

isoTokenShield.name: Guard token editing from Isometric Perspective
isoTokenShield.hint: Keeps the isometric-perspective module out of token configuration windows, where it breaks editing. The map projection and Scene configuration are untouched. Turn it off to reach that module's Isometric tab; no reload.

regionFog.name: Rooms decide what players can see
regionFog.hint: Lights the whole map and lets the module's room fog hide things: the room you are in is clear, rooms you have visited show through a veil, the rest is fogged. Off, Foundry's own vision applies. GMs see everything.

lockPlayerResources.name: Players cannot edit Actions, Hope, Health, Sanity or statistics
lockPlayerResources.hint: Those move through play - spend an action, take a rest, earn a Level Up. On, a player's own edits of them are put back or flagged to the GMs, and their pips are display-only for players; off, they are only listed for the GMs. Items and effects are judged either way, and so is what changed while no GM was connected, when one returns. GMs are unaffected.

friskForce.name: Frisk: forcing after a refusal
friskForce.hint: When off, an open Frisk only asks: a refusal or no answer ends it.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. Crossing into another Scene Region spends the Free Move for that time of day, then an action. Turn off to handle movement by hand.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. Divide the students up in GM panel, Despair Flow.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's single shared Fear bar and gives every Monokuma a Despair pool of their own. Turn off to go back to the system tracker.

enforceIsoWelcome.name: Keep Isometric Perspective's welcome window closed for everyone
enforceIsoWelcome.hint: Isometric Perspective shows its welcome window on every start, and that is a setting of each browser, so turning it off for yourself does nothing for the players. On, the window stays closed on every client and its box disappears from everyone's settings, the GM's included. Off stops holding it: the box comes back and each browser can switch the window on again. Only does anything with Isometric Perspective enabled.

enforceDhWelcome.name: Keep Daggerheart's welcome window closed for everyone
enforceDhWelcome.hint: Daggerheart opens its welcome journal the first time each account starts. On, it stays closed for everyone, the GM included. Off, Daggerheart shows it as before.

enforcePlayerFiles.name: Keep players out of the file browser
enforcePlayerFiles.hint: Players and Trusted Players can neither browse nor upload files, and clicking a portrait opens nothing for them. Pictures already in the world still show. Off, you can give both back in Foundry's permissions.

liveKitInFoundry.name: Voice inside the Foundry window for everyone
liveKitInFoundry.hint: On, every browser joins voice inside the Foundry window and never opens LiveKit's separate window or tab, and LiveKit's box for that disappears from everyone's settings, the GM's included. A change takes effect after a reload. Only does anything with LiveKit AV Client enabled.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Monokuma Legacy only, and on by default there: Press Start 2P on interface chrome - HUD, Despair, character name, statistic labels, tabs. Journals, chat and editable fields keep the normal face so long text stays readable. The Stained Glass theme has its own two faces and ignores this.

language.name: Language
language.hint: This client only. The language of this module's own windows, cards and sheet. The game's proper names - Truth Bullets, Remnants, Despair - stay in English in every language. Takes effect after a reload.

documentLanguage.name: Document language
documentLanguage.hint: The language of the documents the module writes into this world, one for everyone. Windows, cards, and the sheet stay in the Language each browser sets. Set by the primary GM's first start, to their language.

moveAudit.name: A player's token moved through a wall
moveAudit.hint: What happens when a player's token is moved through a wall its character could not pass: a line in the Debug log, or the token put back where it stood, its player told and the GMs warned.
moveAudit.log: Note it in the Debug log

foundryToolWindows.name: The module's windows for Foundry's sidebar and scene controls
foundryToolWindows.hint: On: a GM's Foundry sidebar and scene controls stand in two windows of the module's, Foundry tools and Map tools, opened from the button above the handbooks. Off: they stay where Foundry puts them, and that button is not drawn. A player's screen is the same either way. Takes effect after a reload.

theme.name: Theme
theme.hint: How the module looks on this browser. Stained Glass is the current identity: black broken glass along the screen edges, colour in the seams. Monokuma Legacy is the look before it.

glassPulse.name: Glass pulse
glassPulse.hint: The slow darkening that travels around the frame. Turn it off to keep the glass and stop it breathing. This client only.

highContrast.name: High contrast
highContrast.hint: Brighter fine print, solid hairlines, opaque panels and no blur behind the chrome. Text sizes belong to the Interface scale rather than to this switch, and the map is left alone. On by itself when your system asks for more contrast. This client only.

reducedMotion.name: Reduced motion
reducedMotion.hint: Hold the interface still on this browser, whatever the operating system says. This client only.

hudTicker.name: State name behind the clock
hudTicker.hint: The time of day (or the state that replaces it: Eclipse, Class Trial) as a faint outline running behind the clock. This client only.

bulletSort.name: How Truth Bullets are grouped
bulletSort.hint: Whether your pack is cut into chapters or into rooms. The switch is on the inventory itself, over the evidence; this client only.

glassBlur.name: Glass blurs the map
glassBlur.hint: The glass frosts the map behind it. It is the most expensive thing this theme draws, and it is drawn again every time anything on the screen moves. If the interface stutters or windows are slow to appear, turn this off first - game.drpg.perf() will say what it was costing on this machine. This client only.

messengerSound.name: Messenger sounds
messengerSound.hint: The three sounds the messenger plays - sent, received, a question for the GM. Mutes them on this browser alone; nobody else is affected. This client only.

uiScale.name: Interface scale
uiScale.hint: One factor on the interface, 80% to 140%, this client only. Under Stained Glass the screen's own factor rides under it - 2560 x 1440 is 100%, and a smaller screen draws smaller, down to 70%. Under Monokuma Legacy the slider is the whole factor. It moves this module's type, its panels and its window boxes, and with them Foundry's own chrome and the character sheet; the map is never scaled, and the smallest type stops at 10px.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. This client only.

musicEnabled.name: Music follows the game state
musicEnabled.hint: Swaps the playlist when the Eclipse opens, a trial or investigation begins, the time of day turns, or the game goes on hold. Map the playlists first: GM panel, Sound, Music. The murder row is separate: it plays only for the people in the incident and the GMs, whatever this says.

voiceEnabled.name: Regional voice (needs LiveKit AVClient)
voiceEnabled.hint: Every mapped room becomes its own LiveKit channel - you hear only whoever stands in the room with you. Needs avclient-livekit installed, active and pointed at a working server. Off by default.

voiceTile.name: Voice tile instead of the camera dock
voiceTile.hint: On, the camera dock leaves every screen and the number on the voice tile's speaker shows how many others are in your channel, speaking or not. Foundry's dock is also kept folded, and no camera opens in a window of its own. Off brings Foundry's camera dock back for everyone, folded or open as each browser had it before the tile hid it.

why.noScene: the scene it was on is gone. Propose it again on a scene that stands.
why.twoRooms: the stretch does not join two rooms. Pick a stretch on a wall between two rooms.
why.gmOnly: only a GM's browser can do this. Ask it again from a GM's.
why.noStore: the GMs' record of this season's passages is not loaded. Reload the world, then take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.noBuilder: its builder is no longer a student of this world. Make a new project for another student if it should still happen.
why.idTaken: another passage took its place at the same moment. Take a point off the project and finish it again.
why.breached: that wall already has a breach. Close that breach first, or pick another wall.
why.wholeWall: the stretch takes the whole wall, and nothing of it would stand. Pick a shorter stretch.
why.noBreach: that breach is no longer there: a GM or another project closed it first. Nothing is left to do.
why.wallGone: the wall it was cut from is gone. The room beyond is given back; delete the hole by hand with the walls tool.
why.cannotClose: the passage could not be closed. Close it by hand in the Passages tab.
why.notKnown: the character does not know that passage, or it is closed already. Check it in the Passages tab.
why.isBreach: that is a breach, not a passage. Close the breach gives the wall back.
why.noSide: it has no side in the room where the character stands. Approve it only from a room the passage or the breach opens into.
why.noWall: the wall is gone. Pick the stretch again.
why.taken: the stretch overlaps another passage on that wall. Pick a stretch beside it.
why.levels: a room beside the stretch is on another floor. Pick a stretch on the character's floor.
why.notBetween: the stretch does not stand between two rooms. Pick a stretch of a wall between two rooms.
why.otherRooms: the stretch's two ends stand between different rooms. Pick both ends between the same two rooms.
why.short: the stretch is too short. Pick a longer stretch.
why.door: that wall is a door. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.noMove: that wall does not stop anyone. Pick a stretch of a solid wall.
why.sameEnds: the stretch needs two different ends. Pick it again.
why.offWall: the stretch is no longer on that wall. Pick it again.
why.floor: that wall is not on the character's floor. Pick a wall of that floor.
why.notOwn: the item is not on the builder's own sheet: given away, taken, or a shared sheet's. Approve a repair only for an item the character holds.
why.notRepairable: the item is no usable or tool, or it is whole already. There is nothing to repair.
why.nothingBack: there is nothing to put back. Cut the breach again by hand if it should stand.
why.itemBack: there was nothing to put back on the item.
why.brokenSince: the item was broken or worn again since, and is left as it is.
why.unknown: the module could not say why; the reason is in the GM's console.

tab.intro: A secret passage is one stretch of wall between two rooms that only the students who know it can walk through, at a door's price. To everybody else it is a wall. Each button here takes effect at once; Apply and Cancel do not change it.
tab.startHint: Known again after each season reset. Adding a student here does not give them the passage now.
tab.closeBreachRefused: The breach could not be closed: {why}
tab.wayHint: A tunnel or stairs can go one way only: pick it under its Shape. A passage in a wall always goes both ways.
tab.empty: No secret passages on this map.
tab.stateBroken: The wall moved - pick it again
tab.shared: {players} all play {student}, and each of them learns this passage.
tab.footnote: The Mastermind knows every secret passage and is not listed. Closed keeps who knows it, and the passage is a wall to all of them until it is opened again. Delete forgets the passage and who knew it. Make public: every student knows the passage, and nobody is told; Make secret: only the students listed here know it again.
tab.revokeAsk: {name} is in the {room}, one of the rooms this passage joins. When does it close to them?
tab.revokeNote: Revoke now: it is a wall to them from this moment. Revoke when they leave the room: it stays open to them until they leave the {room}.

tab.revokePublicAsk: {name} knows this passage, and so does every student, while it is public. Revoking closes nothing now: it decides only whether {name} still knows it once you make it secret.

lead.start: No Class Trial is running. Start the Class Trial: the phase moves, the table is told, and the trial opens in discussion.

lead.openAgain: The GM overruled an Objection after its exchange, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the time it had left, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.reopen: The exchange has closed the debate, and the trial is in discussion. Open the debate again with the same question and budget, or send the ballots from The vote.
lead.closeDebate: The debate is open. Close it when the room has argued it out, then send the ballots from The vote.
lead.now: An objection or a rebuttal holds the floor. It runs out on its own; Skip on the bar cuts it short.
lead.vote: The ballots are out. When they are back, Close and count in The vote.
lead.verdict: The vote is counted. Deliver the verdict, then end the chapter.
lead.finishVerdict: The verdict stopped before every step was done. Finish the verdict, then end the chapter.
lead.finishElsewhere: The verdict stopped before every step was done. Only {name} can finish it, so that each of its steps is done once: ask {name}, then end the chapter.
lead.verdictElsewhere: {name} is giving the verdict. If their browser was reloaded inside it, Finish the verdict is on their console; end the chapter once the verdict is done.
lead.chapterEnd: The verdict is in. End the chapter for the reveal and the next chapter.
lead.sentenceWaits: The trial goes on: the sentence is carried out when it ends.
lead.round: A round holds the floor: each speaker in turn. Skip moves to the next speaker; End this mode ends the round.
lead.closing: The Closing Argument holds the floor: confirm or pick its speaker, and after an Objection decide who continues. End the Closing Argument ends it; the vote is the next step.

Vote.finalSentenceMissing: A Final Trial verdict waits to be carried out, but this browser does not hold who was sentenced. Load the GMs' backup on this browser, or give the Final verdict again.

levelUpGranted.one: {n} survivor took their Level Up here: {kind}.
levelUpGranted.other: {n} survivors took their Level Up here: {kind}.

levelUpWaiting.one: {n} survivor's Level Up waits for their player to pick it: {kind}.
levelUpWaiting.other: {n} survivors' Level Ups wait for their players to pick them: {kind}.

blackenedRewarded.one: The Blackened stays anonymous and in play; their {kind} waits for the class's next Level Up.
blackenedRewarded.other: {n} Blackened stay anonymous and in play; each one's {kind} waits for the class's next Level Up.

Vote.newRule: The Blackened introduces one new rule of their choosing, with Monokuma's consent.
Vote.newRuleWritten: The Blackened's new rule has been announced, with no name on it.
Vote.blackenedRuleIntro: The Blackened walked out of this trial, and they get one new rule of their choosing with Monokuma's consent. Type what they asked for.
Vote.blackenedRuleNote: Announced to everyone as one of Monokuma's rules. Nothing in the card says who asked for it, and it goes onto every sheet with the others.
Vote.blackenedRuleUnfound: Dead, and nobody has found the body: {names}. The table does not know of that death, so to the verdict they walked out of this trial: their rule is asked here and their Level Up waits for the class, as a living Blackened's does.
Vote.twoBlackened: This chapter produced {n} Blackened. Name all of them - half an answer is not one.

silent.one: 1 ballot never came back. The count above is out of every ballot issued.
silent.other: {n} ballots never came back. The count above is out of every ballot issued.

Vote.executedIfWrong: Executed instead, if the table got it wrong
Vote.verdictNoteKnown: Getting it right executes the Blackened above - you do not have to name anybody. Getting it wrong executes whoever the table accused, and every Blackened walks away with a Reinforced Level Up. A tie counts as wrong.
Vote.verdictIntroKnown: Only you know whether they got it right. The module remembers who killed - all you have to say is whether the table found them.
Vote.tiedVerdictNote: The vote was tied. A tie is not an answer, so unless something else settled it at the table, this counts as getting it wrong.
Vote.accusedDead: Already dead: {names}. Nobody is executed unless you pick a living student.
Vote.unfoundDead: Dead, and nobody has found the body: {names}. Executing them makes that death the execution, and the table learns of it with the verdict.
Vote.storeNotReady: This browser has not got the GMs' copy of the ballots yet.
Vote.movedOn: The vote has moved on - this window was out of date.
Vote.openNoBallots: The vote is open, round {n}, but this browser holds none of its ballots - wait for the primary GM or Start the vote over.
Vote.executedNote: The verdict has been carried out on you, {name}. Your character is dead.
Vote.verdictStopped: The verdict stopped at: {steps}. Finish the verdict does the rest.
Vote.finishOtherGm: Only {name} can finish the verdict - the GM who gave it while they are connected, otherwise the primary GM - so that each of its steps is done once. Ask {name}.

Music.intro: Pick which playlist plays when. The module never starts a playlist you have not chosen here, and ships no audio of its own.
Music.orderNote: The first state that applies wins, in the order listed. A Class Trial at night uses the trial's playlists; an Eclipse during one uses the Eclipse's.
Music.trialNote: Objection beats the open debate, and the debate beats the trial merely being in session. A rebuttal has no row of its own: the Objection's music keeps playing through it. Each picks a random track when it takes over, never the one it played last. An Objection runs one minute, so give that playlist a short fade.
Music.incidentNote: The murder row plays only in the browsers of the people in the incident and of the GMs, so nobody else learns from the music that a murder is happening. Leave it empty and whatever is playing keeps playing.
Music.fadeNote: Fades are the playlist's own - set Fade Duration on the playlist or on a track, and both directions use it. Put a track on and everything else pauses where it stands, then resumes from there. When a body is found and nothing is mapped to it, the silence stops your own track too.
Music.noPlaylists: This world has no playlists, so there is nothing to map to yet. Make them in the Playlists sidebar; the cue playlist on the Play tab can be made from here.

state.murder: A killing - heard only by the students in it, and the GM
state.bodyFound: A body has been found (silence unless mapped)

Music.playNowNote: Plays one track from the “{name}” playlist on repeat. Whatever is playing pauses where it stands and comes back when you reset.
Music.wasReset: The track is off and whatever it interrupted is back where it left off.
Music.playFailed: That track would not play. See the console.
Music.noSituational: No playlist called “{name}”. Create it below.
Music.situationalMade: “{name}” exists now. Put your scene tracks in it from the Playlists sidebar - stings, reveals, the quiet bits - and they will appear here.
Music.makeFailed: The playlist could not be created. See the console.

diag.clock: Clock: phase={phase} time of day={time} eclipse={eclipse} paused={paused}
diag.cueMissing: MISSING - the Play button has nothing to draw from
diag.onCue: {name} - the cue playlist, never played for a state
diag.noState: No state applies at all - nothing will play.
diag.unmapped: "{state}" is the active state but has no playlist to play, so the music is left alone. Map one: GM panel, Sound, Music.

Cleanup.title: Cleaning up
Cleanup.priceGone: Covering yourself took what this attempt was going to cost. Nothing else was spent.
Cleanup.keptSanity: The attempt keeps its price: the cover story was already told.
Cleanup.withTool: {item} (Tier {tier}) in hand - advantage, and that much off the threshold.
Cleanup.noneReadied: No Cleaning Tool readied. Hold one ready on the Inventory tab first.

blocked.noIncident: No incident is running, so there is nothing to clean up. Stage 6 opens when one ends.
blocked.notYet: The incident is still going on. Clean-up opens the moment it is over - as a Finishing Blow, or by the GM ending it.
blocked.notYours: You are not the one cleaning up this scene.
blocked.monokuma: Monokuma does not clean up after himself. A killing made as a point is meant to be found.

Cleanup.trailNobody: There is nobody left to frame.
Cleanup.moveHint: Spend {n} Sanity to carry the body out of this room. It always leaves an Evident trace - a body cannot be dragged quietly.
Cleanup.bodyNotHere: The body is not in this room. You have to be standing over it to carry it anywhere.
Cleanup.nothingHere: Nothing to clean up in this room.
Cleanup.allReinforced: Every trace here is reinforced. None of it comes off.
Cleanup.rerollLost: A Reroll of a clean-up was not replayed: there was no record here of the attempt it takes back. Its first roll goes back on the card and the Hope is returned.
Cleanup.reinforced: The {what} will not come off. Whatever left it, left it for good.
Cleanup.vanished: The trace you were working on is already gone. The effort still cost you.
Cleanup.freeTonight: Your own scene, tonight: no action, 1 Sanity each.
Cleanup.leftTrace: Your cleaning left a trace of its own.

band.despair: Gone - but you were not careful about it.
band.failure: It will not come off, and you made a mess trying.

Cleanup.gmTool: Readied: {item} (Tier {tier}) - advantage, and {tier} off every threshold below.
Cleanup.gmNoTool: No Cleaning Tool readied - bare hands, no advantage.
Cleanup.gmNothingHere: No traces in the room the killer is standing in.

gmAttemptsLeft.one: Sanity left for {n} more attempt. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you close the murder - closing destroys the crime tool that was used; the cleaning tool goes when the body is found.
gmAttemptsLeft.other: Sanity left for {n} more attempts. Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you close the murder - closing destroys the crime tool that was used; the cleaning tool goes when the body is found.

Cleanup.refundUnheld: {name}'s clean-up asked for {what} back, and the GMs' audit held no record here to check it was paid: nothing was given back. If it was paid, give it back by hand.
Cleanup.freeAttempt: This attempt costs no Sanity: the critical Finishing blow paid for it.
Cleanup.trailPlanted: Planted a Prep Remnant ({visibility}) pointing at {name}.
Cleanup.authorsCopy: You know this trace: it is on your sheet.
Cleanup.bodyMoved: The body has been moved to {room}.
Cleanup.bodyStuck: The body would not move. It still lies where it fell, and no trail of dragging was left.
Cleanup.noBody: There is no body here to move.
Cleanup.bodyNote: {name}'s body was dragged out of here towards {room}.
Cleanup.seenCleaning: {actor} is doing something in {room}, and not hiding it well.
Cleanup.moveIntro: The body is in {room}. Choose where you are dragging it. Costs {n} Sanity.
Cleanup.moveAlwaysTrace: This always leaves an Evident trace behind, whatever the dice say. You cannot drag a corpse quietly. Bedrooms are not on the list: a body behind somebody's locked door names a suspect for you.
Cleanup.bodyNowhere: There is nowhere to take it - no room connects to this one, or the only ones that do are bedrooms.
Cleanup.toolsBroken: {items} is ruined. It is still in your inventory, and it is still evidence.
Cleanup.transformActionHint: Rename it and describe it as something innocent. Threshold three lower than erasing; a critical also makes it quieter and hands back the Sanity. It always ends up a Tamper Remnant.
Cleanup.transformActionIntro: You are not removing this. You are making it read as something else. Write what the next person through the door will find.
Cleanup.reshapeTextPlaceholder: A tin went over during the afternoon. Nobody cleaned it up properly.
Cleanup.reshapeNeedsBoth: Write both a name and a description - an empty lie is not a lie. The window is open again with what you wrote.
Cleanup.reshapeNothingSaid: A reshape needs both a name and a description, and this one did not carry both, so the trace still reads exactly as it did.
Cleanup.reshapeVoided: Taken back by a Reroll or replaced by a later attempt before {name} ruled on it.
Cleanup.reshapeTakenBack: A Reroll or a later attempt took this one's place, so this card no longer rules on anything.
Cleanup.alreadyRuled: This reshape has already been ruled on - by {name}.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedErased: {name} kept your story off the trace. The critical still took it: the trace is gone.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTitle: A trace made to read differently
Cleanup.reshapeRulingQuieter: It rolled well enough to be one band harder to spot as well.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingTies: They are the killer, so approving this also marks the trace as part of the murder.

reshapeRulingCopies.one: Approving leaves the {n} Truth Bullet already copied from it reading as it was found; whoever finds it afterwards reads the new words.
reshapeRulingCopies.other: Approving leaves the {n} Truth Bullets already copied from it reading as they were found; whoever finds it afterwards reads the new words.

Cleanup.reshapeWaiting: You worked it over into “{name}”. Until the GM says otherwise it still reads as it did.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclined: {name} ruled that the trace still says what it said. The turn and the Sanity are spent.
Cleanup.reshapeDeclinedGm: Declined. {name} was told the trace is unchanged.
Cleanup.reshapeRulingGone: That trace is no longer there, so there is nothing to relabel.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsent: A reshaped trace could not be delivered to a thread. Nothing of its story was written on the trace - rule on it in words, and relabel it by hand if you allow it. On the erase road the trace was erased, as the critical bought.
Cleanup.reshapeUnsentPlayer: You worked it over, but your story did not reach the GM. Say it out loud; nothing has been written on the trace.
Cleanup.reshaped: {from} now reads as “{name}”: {band} {kind}. Whoever finds it finds your story, not what was there.
Cleanup.transformActionNote: Whatever you write, the trace becomes a Tamper Remnant - it will admit somebody handled it, and lie about everything else. A critical also makes it one band quieter and hands the Sanity back.
Cleanup.transformIntro: You have time to do more than wipe it. Erase the trace, or leave it saying something else entirely - and, this well rolled, choose how loudly it says it.
Cleanup.transformNote: Nobody sees you decide. Whoever finds it afterwards finds what you left, not what was there. It becomes a Tamper Remnant either way.

Murder.openingReask: Ask for the opening roll again
Murder.openingReaskSent: The invitation to throw the opening roll was sent again.
Murder.openingReaskWait: The invitation was sent a moment ago - give them a few seconds.
Murder.victimNoticedNext: The victim noticed. Nothing happens by itself now: they may use their Free Move, if they still have it, and the incident stays open until you end it from the tracker.
Murder.openIntro: One opening roll, then a turn-based incident. A direct murder opens on the killer's roll; a trap opens on the victim's.
Murder.indirect: Indirect murder - the victim is alone, and the drain is doubled
Murder.indirectCost: A trap is built as projects. Budget about {low}-{high} progress across them, roughly four to six actions, or it costs more to set than it is worth.
Murder.needOne: There must be at least one living student.
Murder.openSelfNote: One name in both seats: this opens as a death by their own hand. There is no Stage 5 - the opening roll decides whether they go through with it, and the incident goes straight to Stage 6.
Murder.killerNotAlive: {name} is named as the killer and is not among the living, so the Killer list shows somebody else. Pick who this murder is for.
Murder.roomsDiffer: {killer} stands in {killerRoom} and {victim} in {victimRoom}. A direct murder happens face to face - bring them together first, or open it anyway if the story already has.
Murder.opened: {killer} is moving on {victim}. The opening roll has gone to {roller}.
Murder.openedSelf: {name} is moving on themselves. The opening roll has gone to them.
Murder.openedSelfNote: Stage 5 is skipped: there is no confrontation to run. If the roll lands, the incident goes straight to Stage 6 - the arrangements they make before dying. They stay alive until you close the incident.
Murder.selfWentThrough: You went through with it. There is no fight to have. Stage 6 is open on your sheet: whatever you leave the room as, you leave it as now.
Murder.resolutionNoteSelf: Stage 6, with nobody left to hide it from but the class. They can see and clean their own traces, and they are still alive to do it - closing the incident is what makes the death real.
Murder.trackerStateSelf: {stage} · no turns - Stage 5 does not run
Murder.afterSelf: By their own hand - nobody else was in the room, and the class has only the scene to go on.
Murder.afterIntroSelf: {name}, by their own hand. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.dayNote: Not night, so the opening roll is unmodified.
Murder.keyCount: This case will leave {n} Key Remnants.
Murder.trackerCastGone: This incident names somebody the world does not have any more ({who}). Nothing can move it on - Close the murder ends it.
Murder.ranOut: {name} is out of Health and out of Sanity. The incident ends and they are dead - no Finishing Blow was needed, and none was earned.
Murder.rerollLost: A Reroll of a crisis action was not replayed: there was no record of it here, or the incident closed or moved on first. Its first roll goes back on the card and the Hope is returned. If the incident closed while it was being taken back, check that action's Remnant and the sheets by hand.
Murder.nobodyElse: There is nobody else alive to walk in.
Murder.endConfirm: Close this murder? The incident state is cleared. Nothing already applied is undone.
Murder.afterTitle: The incident is over - what now
Murder.afterIntro: {killer} against {victim}. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.afterNoRoom: The victim's token is outside every room. Put it where the body is before announcing it.
Murder.afterAutopsy: The autopsy Truth Bullet has not been issued.
Murder.afterDirect: A direct murder - whoever was in the room saw it happen.
Murder.afterIndirect: A trap - nobody saw it, and setting it left traces of its own.
Murder.escapeIntro: {victim} and {third} walked out on {killer}. Nobody died, so there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue and no Class Trial to hold. The incident simply ends.
Murder.escapeRoom: It happened in {room}, and what the fight left behind is still there.
Murder.escapeNoRoom: No room is recorded for this incident, so place whatever it left behind by hand.
Murder.escapeWitness: {victim} and {third} both saw who it was. What they do with that is the table's business.
Murder.escapeKiller: {killer} is not Blackened. Nothing has changed for them except that two people know.
Murder.afterSurvived: {victim} survived the attack by {killer}. Nobody died, so there is no body to announce, no autopsy to issue and no Class Trial to hold, and nobody is Blackened for it. What the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.afterInterrupted: The incident was interrupted before anything was decided - nobody died. There is no body, no autopsy and nobody Blackened for it; what the fight left behind is still where it fell.
Murder.closedVictimYou: The incident is over. You can act again.
Murder.useItemGone: That is not on you any more - nothing to use.
Murder.useItemFumbled: It stays in your pocket, and somebody saw you reaching for it.
Murder.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
Murder.actionHindered: They have made this harder - you roll at disadvantage.
Murder.noStressLeft: Resolution actions cost Sanity, and you have none.
Murder.nothingLeftToSpend: There is nothing left to spend. Sanity and Health are both gone.
Murder.advantageNext: Advantage on the next attempt at this action.
Murder.noKillerLeft: Every killer in this incident is dead. The victim acts alone from here, turn after turn, until the incident is closed.
Murder.killerChooses: Critical - the killer chooses: both marks off Health, or both off Sanity.

hinderedActions.one: {n} of their action at disadvantage for {turns} turns.
hinderedActions.other: {n} of their actions at disadvantage for {turns} turns.

blockedActions.one: {n} of their action shut down entirely for {turns} turns.
blockedActions.other: {n} of their actions shut down entirely for {turns} turns.

Murder.rolesSwapped: The roles are reversed. The killer is the one bleeding now.
Murder.victimDead: The victim is dead. The killer is Blackened.
Murder.resolutionNote: Stage 6. The killer now sees the Remnants on the map and can use resolution actions. Reinforced traces stay put. A crime tool that was used is destroyed.
Murder.thirdIntro: One free choice: get them out with you, take a side, or turn away.
Murder.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
Murder.actionDenied: That action is not open to you now.
Murder.drainStopped: The bleeding stops - no further Health or Sanity is lost this incident.
Murder.indirectBegins: The trap closes. The incident begins with the victim alone, losing 2 a turn.
Murder.tierZeroIntro: {actor} is swinging {item}, a Tier 0 object. A Tier 0 item may count as Tier 1 or 2 when the killer is being creative - how good is this use?
Murder.tierZeroNote: Tier 0 deals 1 damage, Tier 1 deals 2, Tier 2 deals 2 and 3 on a critical. Dismissing this leaves it at Tier 0.
Murder.improvised: Snatched a weapon out of the struggle: {item} (Tier {tier}).
Murder.improvisedNote: Grabbed mid-incident. A crime tool like any other.
Murder.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action - Survive, Escape together, a Finishing blow, or, if you only walked in on it, Averted eyes.
Murder.oneAtATime: There is already an incident running. It has to finish before another can start.
Murder.crisisPrompt: What are you doing about it?
Murder.nothingToDo: There is nothing left for you to do this round.
Murder.actionsLocked: You are in an incident. Everything you can do is behind {tile}; Hope Calls still work.
Murder.thirdJoined: {name} throws in with the killer and stays in the incident.
Murder.thirdLeft: {name} turns away and leaves. They take no part in this.
Murder.thirdEscapedAlone: {name} gets out alone. The victim stays where they are, and {name} takes no part in this any more.
Murder.openingYours: This roll is yours, and it is the only one. It cannot be skipped.
Murder.openingRequired: This roll cannot be skipped. Throw it.
Murder.openingDeclined: {name} did not throw the opening roll. Stage 4 cannot be skipped: ask again from the Incident tracker, or end the incident.
Murder.openingRemnantNote: {name} sensed the attempt ({band}). Something of the struggle was left to notice.

leftRemnants.one: Leaves a trace behind, and the killer cannot wipe it.
leftRemnants.other: Leaves {n} traces behind, and the killer cannot wipe them.

Murder.keyRemnantsStale: The roles reversed, so the case changed: the {n} Key Remnants were planned around a killer who is now the victim. Write {n} new ones before the Investigation - the count came off the opening roll and has not changed.
Murder.nightNoteDirect: It is night: the killer's opening roll has advantage.
Murder.nightNoteIndirect: It is night: the victim's opening roll has disadvantage.
Murder.betrayalNote: {third} walked in on this and is still standing. They may turn on {killer} until the day ends. Outside an Eclipse it is the one killing in the game that needs no declaration in advance; in one it is declared, and opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalIntro: {third} kills {killer}. This closes as a second murder, with {third} as the killer and {killer} as the victim - a fresh incident from the opening roll, not a continuation of the one that just ended.
Murder.betrayalRule: Two bodies in one day, so the Class Trial has two killings to untangle. Whoever is Blackened for the first is not automatically Blackened for the second. You have until the end of the day to decide.
Murder.betrayalConfirmEclipse: An Eclipse is running, so the betrayal is declared now and opens when the Eclipse ends, like any action declared in one. It costs an action, and the action stays spent even if the betrayal cannot open then.
Murder.betrayalParked: Your betrayal is declared. It opens when the Eclipse ends.
Murder.betrayalAnnounce: A second incident opens on {killer} - the betrayal.
Murder.betrayalRefused: The betrayal could not open: {why}. It stays on offer until the day ends.

betrayalWhy.spent: it is no longer on offer
betrayalWhy.failed: the GM's client could not open it
betrayalWhy.trial: a Class Trial is in session
betrayalWhy.dead: one of the two is no longer alive

Murder.victimUnderAttackBy: {killer} is moving on you. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours. On your character sheet, under Actions, press Fight back.
Murder.victimTrapSprung: The trap closes. You did not see it in time. The incident has begun and the first turn is yours - on your character sheet, under Actions, press Fight back.
Murder.offTurn: It is their turn. Your crisis actions open when it comes back to you.
Murder.breakdownDisadvantage: You are in Breakdown, so this roll is at disadvantage until some Sanity comes back.
Murder.gmPicksTrait: Rolls: {traits} - the GM picks one. Tell them in your thread what you do.
Murder.youPickTrait: Rolls: {traits} - Resolve is armed, so you pick one in the roll window.
Murder.criticalChoiceIntro: The blow lands exactly where you wanted it. Take both marks off the same place - their body, or their nerve.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillers: {victim} has nothing left. {killers} are both in this.
Murder.ranOutTwoKillersNote: End it now and the incident moves to the clean-up. Keep going and the turn order carries on - nobody loses a turn they were owed, and you can end it from the tracker whenever you like.
Murder.crowded: {name} walked in on top of {third}. Four people in one room is not a murder anybody can carry out - the incident is cancelled.
Murder.crowdedNote: Nobody dies. What the fight already did stands: the wounds, the Sanity, and anything it left on the floor.
Murder.freeResolution: You stopped them cold. Take Survive or Role reversal this turn - no roll, it simply works.
Murder.castMissingHere: This browser holds no cast for the running incident, so its turn cannot be worked out here. Enter the cast by hand (the case's health check), or let the GM whose browser holds it act.
Murder.castNotArrived: The other GMs' copies of the incident's cast have not arrived on this browser yet: try again in a moment.
Murder.deniedByIncident: The incident has taken this one away from you.

Investigation.neverOnePerson: A clue narrows the circle, it never names a name: a Key Remnant points at half the cast at most, an ordinary trace at 2-4 people. The last step from circle to name belongs to the trial.
Investigation.plannerIntro: {n} clues for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}-{max} people.
Investigation.placedMeanwhile: Another GM placed this row's Key Remnant while the window was open, so nothing more was placed.
Investigation.tokenGone: Its Remnant is gone from the map
Investigation.keyRetyped: Its Remnant is no longer a Key Remnant

keyOffPlan.one: One more found Key Remnant is not on the plan and counts toward the four: {names}.
keyOffPlan.other: {n} more found Key Remnants are not on the plan and count toward the four: {names}.

Investigation.tooThin: Only {found} Key Remnants have been found. The minimum is {min} - below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.
Investigation.breakdownTooltip: What each student's Truth Bullets really are, kind by kind, by the GMs' answer key - not what their holders were shown.
Investigation.newTraceIntro: A trace you are simply stating exists. It is dropped at a random spot inside the room, exactly like a planned clue - move the token afterwards if the spot matters.
Investigation.newTraceTied: Part of this murder (survives the chapter-end sweep)
Investigation.newTraceNote: The name and the description are what a student reads when they find it; what analysis reveals waits for their Analyze. Your note stays yours.
Investigation.newTraceBadType: That is not a kind of trace this module knows.
Investigation.newTraceUnfindable: Nothing can find a trace of that kind at that difficulty - Observe has no number for it.
Investigation.noRooms: This scene has no rooms on it yet, so there is nowhere to put a trace. Draw the regions first - Room setup explains how.
Investigation.createNote: Place puts a row's Key Remnant on the map at once, in the room you pick: reinforced, tied to the crime, somewhere inside the room, with the words typed on its row. A row already on the map has no Place button.
Investigation.keyDcNote: A Key Remnant is the easiest thing in a room to notice, and how easy depends on where you put it, not on the scale above: {list}. Ordinary evidence in the same band is three to six harder. The scale is how much a clue gives away.
Investigation.keyLimitLine: {used} of {limit} used this chapter - the minimum is {min}.
Investigation.keyLimitOverride: Create more than the opening roll allows

savedOver.one: One field had changed elsewhere while this window was open, and was not saved: {list}. The window shows what it holds now; type yours again if it should stand.
savedOver.other: {n} fields had changed elsewhere while this window was open, and were not saved: {list}. The window shows what they hold now; type yours again if they should stand.

Investigation.createHereIntro: They named a point of interest and you have decided there is something there. This puts it on the map, and can hang it on one of the five clues you planned.

unfoundKeys.one: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants - one short. {despair} Despair to each pool: {who}.
unfoundKeys.other: The investigation turned up {found} of {bar} Key Remnants - {n} short. {despair} Despair to each pool: {who}.

Investigation.keyPublicNote: Name and Player description are what a finder holds the moment they pick it up; What analysis reveals waits for their Analyze. The same three fields the Traces tab edits. Your note stays yours.

leftoverKeys.one: {n} Key Remnant from an earlier chapter is still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see it; clear it at the end of a chapter or attach it here.
leftoverKeys.other: {n} Key Remnants from an earlier chapter are still on the map. This chapter's plan cannot see them; clear them at the end of a chapter or attach them here.

Investigation.chargeTooLate: The clock has already moved to chapter {now}, and the last case was chapter {was}'s: this chapter has no case of its own to count unfound Key Remnants against, so nothing was charged.

Vault.foundStashPending: You find somebody's stash. What comes out of it settles in a moment.
Vault.foundStashNothing: You find somebody's stash, but nothing from it stays in your hands.
Vault.handsFull: Your hands are full: what you found in the stash stays where it was.
Vault.stowTooltip: Put this in your stash (you must be in the room)
Vault.takeTooltip: Take this back out (you must be in the room)
Vault.notHere: Your stash is in {room} - stand there to reach it.
Vault.noStashOnScene: You have no stash on this scene.
Vault.handFirst: {item} cannot be held ready, and only one {group} may be stowed. Take a working one in hand first.
Vault.noBullets: Truth Bullets are what you know, not things in a stash.
Vault.full: {room} is full. A stash holds {limit} things - take something out before putting something in.
Vault.overflowed: Your hands were full, so {item} went into your stash. Your {category} limit is unchanged.
Vault.foundInStash: Hidden in this room, you find {item}.
Vault.rifledAgain: You have already been through {who}'s stash this time of day. Try it again at the next time of day.
Vault.noticed: Something has been moved in your stash, and something is missing from it. You have no idea whose hands have been in it.
Vault.stashesIntro: Who has a stash in which room, and whether it is hidden. Click a cell to cycle: none, open, hidden. A bedroom gives its owner an open stash automatically - its cell is shaded - and you can take that away here.
Vault.stashesNote: An open stash is open: anyone standing in the room can go through it for free and take one thing, once each time of day. A hidden one has to be found first: with a Search at a penalty, or with an Analyze of 16 or more. A stash in somebody else's room does NOT come with a key to it.
Vault.stashCycle: Click to cycle: none / open / hidden

stashNotEmpty.one: {name} has one thing in the stash in {room} - take it out before removing it.
stashNotEmpty.other: {name} has {n} things in the stash in {room} - take them out before removing it.

Vault.manageIntro: Everything a room is, one kind of fact per tab. Apply saves every tab at once, whichever one is showing.
Vault.manageNote: A favoured category gives advantage to anyone searching here for it; a bad one gives disadvantage, and a category can never be both. A room with no table of its own falls through to the global pool, so half-finished setup is fine.
Vault.bedroomsIntro: Whose bedroom each room is. One student, one bedroom. Whether a stash is hidden is set on the Stashes tab.
Vault.doorsIntro: Which doors are locked right now, and which start a season locked. A season reset puts every door back to its start column.
Vault.roomRatio: {rooms}. Living students: {living} ({per} rooms each). This season was built on {target} per student, so this cast wants {want}.

roomCensus.one: {n} shared room (bedrooms and “No privacy” rooms left out, locked rooms counted)
roomCensus.other: {n} shared rooms (bedrooms and “No privacy” rooms left out, locked rooms counted)

roomCensusUndecided.one: Not counted yet: {n} region nobody has decided, ticked as a suggestion - Apply makes it a room.
roomCensusUndecided.other: Not counted yet: {n} regions nobody has decided, ticked as suggestions - Apply makes them rooms.

Vault.searchIntro: What searching each room draws from, how many search tokens it has left, and what it is a sensible place to look for.
Vault.placeColumn: Good or bad place to look for
Vault.placeCycle: Click to cycle: neither / good place / bad place
Vault.noRooms: This scene has no room regions yet.
Vault.noneSet: No bedrooms have been assigned yet.
Vault.twoRooms: {name} cannot have two bedrooms ({a} and {b}). Pick one.
Vault.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. Long tables, a serving hatch, and a smell of bleach nobody can place.
Vault.descriptionIntro: Describe in your own words what each room looks like, and add a picture if you want. Whoever stands in a room sees it on their room tile.
Vault.descriptionNote: Plain text, shown as typed; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Pictures come only from this game's files, or on The Forge from your Assets Library. Every browser holds the descriptions and pictures of all rooms, so keep a room's secrets in its stashes and traces.
Vault.imageRefused: {room}: the picture was not saved. Pick a jpg, png, webp or avif from this game's files, or on The Forge from your Assets Library.
Vault.fogIntro: Which rooms each character has already discovered on this scene. The room they are standing in is always clear; this is only about rooms they have BEEN to, which show as a dim veil rather than full fog.
Vault.fogUncovered: {pct}% of this scene's surface belongs to no room region at all - it will show as permanent fog rather than a wall gap, which usually means a room still needs drawing.
Vault.fogNote: Discover all / Hide all tick or clear every checkbox above for every character at once. Nothing changes until you press Apply. The individual checkboxes are for one room, one character.
Vault.inspectNote: Take things out from Give / take items - a stashed item is an ordinary item on its owner's sheet.
Vault.rifleIntro: Stashes you can reach in {room}: {who}. Take one thing from each, once each time of day.
Vault.rifleNote: Free. A hidden stash you have not found needs a Search instead.
Vault.noOpenStashHere: There is no open stash in this room.
Vault.openStashNote: You can take one thing from each stash listed here, once each time of day.
Vault.keyDescription: Opens the door to {room}, which belongs to {owner}. Share a copy to let somebody else in.
Vault.keyShared: {who} gave you a copy of the key to {room}.
Vault.keyGave: {who} now has a copy of your key to {room}.
Vault.keyMissing: The door to {room} is locked. You do not have that key.
Vault.giveKeyNote: A copy - the owner keeps theirs. Only rooms that belong to somebody are listed: a room with no owner has no door to unlock.
Vault.keyDuplicatesTaken: {actor} held more than one key to {room}: one is kept, and the extra copies were taken.
Vault.keyTakenGm: {actor} no longer holds the key to {room}: the room is not theirs any more.
Vault.keyTakenBack: Your key to {room} was taken back: the room is not yours any more.
Vault.keyCopiesGm: Copies of the key to {room} are still held by {holders}. They open its door for its new owner too; take them away by hand if they should go with the room.
Vault.noKeysToGive: No keys left to hand over - this character already holds one for every bedroom that has an owner.
Vault.hasEveryKey: {name} already holds a key to every bedroom that has an owner.
Vault.onlyOwnBedroom: The only bedroom with an owner is {name}'s own. There is no key to give.
Vault.noKeysToTake: {actor} holds no key to anybody else's room.
Vault.lockedAtStartHint: Whether this door is locked when a season begins. A season reset puts every door back to this.
Vault.isRoomHint: Whether this region is a room. A region with a Teleport or level-change behaviour, or one a player drew, cannot be one.
Vault.notSharedHint: Leave this region out of the rooms-per-player count. Changes no rule.
Vault.notSharedNote: “No privacy” is for corridors, stairwells and anywhere nobody can talk privately. It changes only the room count - the ratio line above, the same row in Season setup and Pre-season checks; movement, searching, rests and fog are unaffected. Bedrooms are already excluded, by having an owner.
Vault.neighboursHint: The rooms this one has a door to, separated by commas. Blank: its walls decide (the greyed names).
Vault.neighboursNote: “Neighbours” is where a door overrules the map: list the rooms this one opens into, separated by commas. Two rooms are connected when either lists the other, both ways. A room with a list is connected to nothing else, and a room beside it cannot walk in unless one of the two lists the other. Left blank, a room's neighbours are the rooms without a list whose walls share an edge with its own (a corner is not enough), and every room that lists it. A room the lists and the walls leave with no neighbour has no door out. A room that has no list, is in no list and touches no other room, not even at a corner, is not checked: a crossing from it may go to any room.
Vault.neighboursUnknown: {room}: no room on this scene is named {names}. Kept in its Neighbours, where it connects nothing.

Chapter.keepBullets: Keep their Truth Bullets (not a killing-game death)
Chapter.deathNote: Their Truth Bullets are destroyed, carried and stashed alike, and that cannot be undone. Everything else stays on the body to be found, and the dead move none of it. The dead stop counting as being in the room: no witnessing, no handovers, no murder blocked.
Chapter.vaultPending: A stash is still their own sheet, so stashed bullets are in the count above and everything else they put away stays there to be found.
Chapter.stageSixTitle: That was the victim of the incident
Chapter.stageSixIntro: {victim} is the victim of the incident {killer} is in, and the incident is still running.
Chapter.stageSixWhat: Moving it to Stage 6 lets {killer} see the traces they left and spend Sanity trying to erase them. The incident stays open until you close it, so nothing is announced yet.
Chapter.revived: {name} is no longer marked dead. The Truth Bullets that died with them do not come back.
Chapter.deadPanelNote: The dead take no actions and spend no Hope. You keep your sheet and your voice at the table. Brought back as a Monocub, this panel becomes Move and Confusion.
Chapter.deadCannotAct: {name} is dead and cannot take actions.
Chapter.keepSecretUntilFound: Keep it the GMs' until the body is found: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets stay until then
Chapter.keptUntilFound: Kept by the GMs until the body is found or you make it known in the Players window. The table sees nothing yet: no flag, no marker, and their Truth Bullets are still on the sheet.
Chapter.nobodyFoundYou: Nobody has found your body yet.
Chapter.youFoundBody: In {room} you find the body of {name}. Nobody else has seen it yet, and nothing is announced.

deathsStillSecret.one: {n} death nobody has found is still the GMs' alone. Until you make it known in the Players window, this trial treats that student as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killer, who counts as a Blackened only for a death the table knows.
deathsStillSecret.other: {n} deaths nobody has found are still the GMs' alone. Until you make them known in the Players window, this trial treats those students as living - they vote and level up with the class - and does not ask for their killers, who count as Blackened only for a death the table knows.

Chapter.bodyAnnouncedAlready: {name}'s body was already announced in this chapter, so nothing was announced again. To announce another body in that room, leave the body unnamed.
Chapter.bodyPrimaryOnly: Only the primary GM, {name}, can announce a body, so that one browser decides which bodies the table has found. Ask {name}, or announce it when you are the only GM connected.
Chapter.bodyNotPublished: {name}'s death could not be made known to the table, so the discovery does not name them and the death is still the GMs' alone. Make it known in the Players window.
Chapter.noRooms: This scene has no room regions to gather anyone into.
Chapter.bodyNote: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change until you start the Investigation.
Chapter.bodyNoteLater: Everyone is called to the room. The phase does not change.
Chapter.bodyNoteTraces: Then you are asked which traces left while somebody gathered tools belong to this murder.
Chapter.bodyFound: A body has been found in {room}.
Chapter.bodyCalled: Everyone is called to the scene. The Investigation has not started yet.

promoted.one: {n} trace now counts as evidence of this murder.
promoted.other: {n} traces now count as evidence of this murder.

Chapter.promoteIntro: These Prep traces were left while somebody gathered tools. Most mean nothing. Tick the ones that belong to this killing.
Chapter.promoteNote: Ticked traces stop being doubtful: they count as evidence tied to the crime, and a Faint clear will not take them. Leave the rest and they stay Faint.
Chapter.endIntro: Chapter {chapter} is wrapping up. Tick what should happen.
Chapter.optReveal: Reveal what the Truth Bullets really are, with their readings ({n} to reveal)
Chapter.revealKeeps: Faint Truth Bullets are not revealed, except that every Final, Faint or not, shows its kind without its reading: both stay with their holders, still to be analysed, in the next chapter too.
Chapter.endNote: Revealing the types is permanent, and so are the three clean-ups above. Nothing else here deletes anything.
Chapter.lastChapter: Chapter {n} is the last of a season. Reset the season from Between sessions rather than moving on to chapter {next}.
Chapter.optNextMorning: Open the next chapter on the morning of day {day}, with actions and search tokens refilled
Chapter.moved: The clock now reads chapter {chapter}, session {session}.

typeless.one: 1 Truth Bullet not analysed has no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch it - {who} holds it. Take it, and give one with its type from Give / take items.
typeless.other: {n} Truth Bullets not analysed have no real type recorded, so revealing cannot touch them - held by {who}. Take them, and give ones with their types from Give / take items.

Chapter.optSweep: Collect the Truth Bullets ({n} would go, Faint and Final stay)
Chapter.optFaint: Clear the Faint Remnants ({n} would go)
Chapter.optKeys: Take this chapter's Key Remnants off the map ({n})

doneKeys.one: Took {n} Key Remnant off the map.
doneKeys.other: Took {n} Key Remnants off the map.

Chapter.optEndTrial: Close the trial and return everyone to Daily Life
Chapter.finalTruthMissing: No Final Truth Remnant was placed this chapter. One a chapter points at the Mastermind: place it from The case > Investigation, on the Final Truth Remnants tab.
Chapter.doneEndTrial: Closed the trial; the campaign is back in Daily Life.
Chapter.doneNextMorning: The next chapter opens on the morning of day {day}, with actions and search tokens refilled.
Chapter.doneInvestigationOver: The Investigation is over; the campaign is back in Daily Life.
Chapter.endTwice: This End of chapter window was opened on chapter {chapter}, session {session}, day {day}, and the clock's chapter, session or day has moved since - by another End of chapter, by Edit campaign, or by the time of day turning into a new day. Nothing was done: open End of chapter again to choose against the clock as it stands now.
Chapter.endPhaseMoved: This End of chapter window was opened in {opened}, and the clock has read {now} since - the phase changed after the window was drawn, so what it offered to close is not what is sitting now. Nothing was done: open End of chapter again to choose against the clock as it stands now.
Chapter.endPrimaryOnly: Only the primary GM, {name}, can end the chapter, so that one browser counts it once. Ask {name}, or end it when you are the only GM connected.
Chapter.endFailed: The end of the chapter did not finish: {steps}. Everything else was done - finish those by hand rather than ending the chapter again.
Chapter.endStopped: The phase changed from {opened} to {now} while the chapter was ending, so these did not run: {steps}. What ran stays done - finish the rest by hand when the table is ready for it, rather than ending the chapter again.

step.keys: taking the Key Remnants off the map

TrialScene.castUnavailable: The trial opened and nobody in the trial hall was shown: the GMs' choice of its tokens had not reached this client yet. Show them by hand on the hall's scene.
TrialScene.duplicateToken: More than one token in the trial hall stands for the same character, and only the first was shown. Kept hidden: {names}.
TrialScene.playerTokenCreated: {user} made a token in the trial hall: {name}. It is hidden - showing the hall's tokens is the GM's - and stays where it is; the next trial treats it as any token of the hall.
TrialScene.playerTokenDeleted: {user} deleted a token from the trial hall: {name}. If the module made it, it makes it again the next time the trial opens; if a GM placed it, put it back by hand if the trial needs it.
TrialScene.hiddenPutBack: {user} changed whether {name} is hidden in the trial hall. Showing and hiding the hall's tokens is the GM's, so it was put back as the GMs left it.
TrialScene.noSchool: The Class Trial ended, but no school scene is linked and the scene the trial opened from is gone, so the table stays in the trial hall and its tokens stay as they are. Activate a scene by hand.

notMoved.one: {n} living student could not be moved and stays where they stood: {names}. Move them by hand.
notMoved.other: {n} living students could not be moved and stay where they stood: {names}. Move them by hand.

carryUnfinished.one: {n} student carried out of the Class Trial stands twice - the copy and the token it was made from, which was not deleted: {names}. Delete the one you do not want.
carryUnfinished.other: {n} students carried out of the Class Trial stand twice - each a copy and the token it was made from, which was not deleted: {names}. Delete the ones you do not want.

hiddenHere.one: {n} living student's token in the room is hidden, and a shown token of theirs stays on another scene: {names}.
hiddenHere.other: {n} living students' tokens in the room are hidden, and shown tokens of theirs stay on other scenes: {names}.

tokensStay.one: {n} living student in the room still has a token on another scene, left where it stood: {names}.
tokensStay.other: {n} living students in the room still have a token on another scene, left where it stood: {names}.

TrialScene.scenesIntro: Link the two scenes of the season once: the school, where the students live, and the trial hall, a scene of its own for the Class Trial. Opening the trial takes every browser to the hall and gives each student ticked below a token there - the GMs' own token in the hall if there is one, else one the module makes; ending it takes the module's tokens away, remembering where they stood, hides the GMs' and takes the table back - End the trial to the room you choose, with the living students who took part from every scene with rooms, any other road to the school. The module never deletes a token the GMs placed in the hall.

hallRoom.legend: The trial hall on the room tile
hallRoom.hint: Everybody sees these on the room tile during the Class Trial. Write nothing secret here.
hallRoom.name: Name

TrialScene.reveal: Ticked: they take part - a token in the hall when the Class Trial opens (the GMs' own if there is one, else one the module makes), and brought to the room End the trial chooses. Unticked: no token of theirs is shown, and they are not moved after the trial - a test student, or a player nobody should see yet.
TrialScene.noCast: The world has no student or Monokuma yet.
TrialScene.sameScene: The school and the trial hall are the same scene. Pick two different scenes - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.hallInTrial: A Class Trial is running in the linked trial hall. End the trial before you link another hall or unlink this one - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.hallFirstInTrial: A Class Trial is running without a trial hall. Link one after the trial ends - Apply waits until then.
TrialScene.noSchoolLinked: No school is linked: ending the trial goes back to the scene that was active when it opened.
TrialScene.hallHasRooms: This scene has regions marked as rooms: {names}. In the trial hall they are not rooms - is this the school's map? Regions not marked as rooms are fine here.
TrialScene.duplicateInHall: More than one token in the hall stands for the same character, and a trial shows only the first. The others: {names}.
TrialScene.unlinkedToken: Tokens in the hall not linked to their character: {names}. The dead overlay and the player's control are read off the character, so link each to its character.
TrialScene.hallDark: The trial hall still has Foundry's token vision on, its global light off or its exploration fog on. For everybody to see the whole hall, tick "Prepare the hall" in Room Setup's Scenes tab and press Apply.
TrialScene.prepare: Prepare the hall on Apply: Foundry's exploration fog off, token vision off, global light on - everybody sees the whole hall.
TrialScene.prepareVoice: Also switch Proximity Voice Chat off in the hall (in the trial everybody is in one voice room)
TrialScene.noWayBack: No school is linked and the scene the trial opened from is gone, so the table stays in the trial hall. Link a school in Room Setup's Scenes tab.
TrialScene.phaseSwitchesScene: It also takes every browser to the trial hall, {hall}, and places the tokens of the students chosen for it.
TrialScene.castPickHeading: Who takes part in this trial

notPlaced.one: The trial hall has no token for {n} of the trial's cast, so the trial cannot show them: {names}. The module makes none for Monokuma, and one it could not make is in the console - place one on the hall's scene by hand.
notPlaced.other: The trial hall has no token for {n} of the trial's cast, so the trial cannot show them: {names}. The module makes none for Monokuma, and one it could not make is in the console - place one for each on the hall's scene by hand.

Trial.presentTooltip: Present - put this on the table for everyone to see.
Trial.presentIntro: You are about to show {name} ({type}) to everyone. Only what you can see goes on the card. Never the GM's notes.
Trial.commentPlaceholder: e.g. This is why the timeline does not work.
Trial.presentNote: Present puts this on the table for everyone to see. It costs nothing, and nobody's turn to speak changes. To take the floor in the debate, press OBJECTION! on the HUD.
Trial.notInTrial: Evidence is presented in a Class Trial. Outside one, share a copy instead.

Trial.logSummary: {total} presented this chapter, {objections} of them as an Objection that took the floor.

Trial.objectionRefunded: Your Objection did not take the floor: {why} What you paid ({what}) was given back, and the card is marked as refused.
Trial.objectionRefundLost: Your Objection did not take the floor: {why} What you paid ({what}) could not be given back - tell the GM. The card is marked as refused.
Trial.objectionNotYours: That Objection was posted by somebody who does not own {name}, so the floor did not move.
Trial.objectionNoItem: That Objection named no evidence, so the floor did not move.
Trial.deadCannotPresent: {name} is dead, and the dead neither present evidence nor object.
Trial.presentByButton: Evidence is presented with Present on your sheet, and the GM's browser posts its card. That card was not posted that way, so nobody was shown it.
Trial.presentWithAnalysis: Show it with my Analyze result
Trial.presentWithoutNote: Unticked, the card and everybody's copy show it as never analysed: no reading, no type it turned out to be.
Trial.presentCopy: {who} presented {name}. A copy, as it was shown, is now on your sheet.
Trial.logEmpty: Nothing has been presented this chapter yet.
Trial.objectionNobody: There is nobody else left to object to.
Trial.objectionWarning: Once your Truth Bullet is on the table, the debate is yours: {objection} seconds in which only you may speak, then {rebuttal} seconds of rebuttal with the one you objected to.
Trial.actionsLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Only Analyze and an Objection are open - and your Hope Calls.
Trial.moveLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Nobody leaves the courtroom until it ends.
Trial.callsLocked: The Class Trial is in session. Despair Calls wait for it to end.
Trial.objectionNoFloor: The debate is not open, so there is nothing to interrupt. Show the evidence instead.

Trial.objectionNoGm: No GM is connected, so nobody can hand over the floor. Put the evidence on the table instead.
Trial.objectionOutside: Objection only in a Class Trial.
Trial.objectionDuringObjection: Somebody else's Objection is running. Wait for their minute and the rebuttal that follows it.

Trial.objectionByButton: An Objection is raised with OBJECTION! on the HUD, not from the sheet. Press it, then choose your Truth Bullet.
Trial.objectionWithdrawn: withdrawn - no Truth Bullet was presented
Trial.objectionPickIntro: Your Objection is aimed at {target}. Choose the Truth Bullet that proves it.
Trial.objectionPickCount: {seconds} s left to choose. When they run out the Objection is withdrawn, and what you paid is not given back.
Trial.objectionAtNow: OBJECTION! at {target}, who is speaking now.
Trial.objectionAtLast: OBJECTION! at {target}, the last to speak.

Trial.objectionNoRoom: The GM is not connected to a voice channel, so name whom you contradict.
Trial.objectionFailed: Your Objection did not go through. Press OBJECTION! again, or tell the GM.
Trial.objectionSpeakerOnly: In {mode}, an Objection can only be aimed at whoever is speaking.

turn.title: Your turn - {seconds} s

Handover.alreadyHasKey: {who} already has a key to that room.
Handover.stashed: {name} is in a stash, not in your hands. Take it out first.
Handover.shareTooltip: Share a copy with someone in this room

Handover.giveIntro: Who do you hand {name} to? You are in {room}.

Handover.changedMidway: “{name}” changed on {from}'s sheet while it was on its way to {to} - used, broken or gone. Nothing changed hands.
Handover.changedMidwayKept: “{name}” changed on {from}'s sheet while it was on its way to {to} - used, broken or gone - and the copy could not be taken back. There is one too many now - remove it from {to}'s sheet.

gaveOne.one: You hand {who} one {name}. You still have one.
gaveOne.other: You hand {who} one {name}. You still have {left}.

Handover.answerKeyMissing: {name} cannot be handed over now: what it really is is not on the GM's browser. The GM can bring it back from a backup (Restore the case).

Observe.sent: The GM is judging what you found.

Observe.projectFound: Under the surface of the room, somebody has been building: {name}. You know about it now, and you can see how far along it is.
Observe.critIdentified: You found it, and you know what kind of trace it is.
Observe.whichRemnant: Which Remnant are they closest to?
