Observe.pickGone: Nobody is waiting on this Observe any more: its player stopped waiting, or another GM answered it first.
Observe.describeIntro: {actor} found something in {room}. Name it as they would, and say what they see.
Observe.critPrompt: Critical - the category is identified for them, and they have earned a substantial hint.
Observe.resolveLost: {name} rolled {total} on an Observe and this browser has no record of what they were looking at. Nothing was found and nothing was charged - the action is gone. Ask them what they declared, and hand the find over by hand if there was one.
Observe.resolveLostOwner: Your Observe could not be scored: the GM's browser has no record of what you were looking at. Nothing was found and nothing was marked. Tell them what you declared.
Observe.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for an Observe with no record here. Score the new number against the same trace by hand, and take back the Truth Bullet if it no longer fits.
Observe.alreadyHeld: You already hold a Truth Bullet of this trace.
Observe.alreadyDescribed: This trace already has a name, and every observer is told the same one - two names for one object is a contradiction the trial has to spend itself resolving. A critical buys a bigger hint, not a new name: add it below.
Observe.generalHint: Sweep the room for whatever is easiest to spot.
Observe.nonObviousHint: Look past the obvious: the hardest thing here, and whatever does not belong in this room at all.
Observe.followTracesHint: Retrace your own steps and look for what you left behind.
Observe.specificHint: Say what you are looking for. The GM decides what your gaze lands on.
Observe.anythingHint: Something that is not a trace - a person, a machine, the weather. The GM rules on it.

TruthBullet.title: Truth Bullet
TruthBullet.noneToTake: {actor} is not carrying any Truth Bullets.
TruthBullet.remnantNote: The bullet copies the trace: type, difficulty, room, the action that left it, and whether it is tied to the murder. The marker becomes visible to whoever holds it and nobody else. Renaming it here renames the trace.
TruthBullet.remnantEmpty: No Remnants on any scene. Place one on a map, or write a bullet by hand on the other tab.
TruthBullet.remnantGone: That Remnant is no longer on the map.
TruthBullet.needsName: The Truth Bullet needs a name.
TruthBullet.name: Name - this is what the player sees
TruthBullet.shown: What the player is told it is
TruthBullet.shownAuto: By the rules - Key and Final show their kind and keep their analysis for an Analyze, Autopsy arrives whole, the rest start Neutral
TruthBullet.shownReal: The real type - no analysis needed
TruthBullet.visibility: How hard the original was to spot
TruthBullet.visibilityTooltip: How visible the original Remnant was. This sets the difficulty of analyzing it.
TruthBullet.faintField: Faint - doubtful, and the first thing a GM's clear takes
TruthBullet.tiedField: Tied to the murder - floats to the top of the pack once identified
TruthBullet.faintTooltip: Doubtful. Survives into the next session and can be analyzed again.
TruthBullet.lockedTooltip: Analysis failed this chapter. Try next chapter, or hand a copy on.
TruthBullet.playerTextPlaceholder: What the person who found it actually sees.
TruthBullet.analyzedTextPlaceholder: What the lab says that the eye could not - whose blood, which cuff, what the smell is.
TruthBullet.analyzedTextNote: Optional. Only a student who passes Analyze on this trace ever reads it; leave it empty and Analyze still names the category.
TruthBullet.gmNote: Note for the GM (never shown to the player)
TruthBullet.gmNotePlaceholder: What it really means for the case.
TruthBullet.secretNote: The real type and your note stay on the GM side. They never reach the player's item.
TruthBullet.whereToFind: It is in your inventory, under Truth Bullets.
TruthBullet.reallyTooltip: GM only - what this Truth Bullet actually is.
TruthBullet.autopsyHint: The state of the body - the time it was discovered, and the cause of death. Handed out at the start of every Investigation, never rolled for. Everyone is ticked; untick the victim.
TruthBullet.autopsyTextPlaceholder: Time of discovery, cause of death, and anything else the body shows.
TruthBullet.autopsyNobody: Nobody is ticked, so there is nobody to give it to.

autopsyIssued.one: Autopsy Truth Bullet issued to {n} character.
autopsyIssued.other: Autopsy Truth Bullet issued to {n} characters.

TruthBullet.migratedTitle: Truth Bullets brought up to date

migrated.one: {n} Truth Bullet made before this version now carries a type, a visibility and a chapter. Its real type could not be recovered, so it is recorded as Neutral - correct it from Give / take items if it matters.
migrated.other: {n} Truth Bullets made before this version now carry a type, a visibility and a chapter. Their real type could not be recovered, so each is recorded as Neutral - correct the ones that matter from Give / take items.

TruthBullet.editReverted: {player} changed their Truth Bullet “{bullet}” - what it says or what it is. The change was put back: only a GM writes on evidence.
TruthBullet.editUnrestored: {player} changed the Truth Bullet “{bullet}”, and there was no record of it to put it back from. The change stayed on that one copy and went no further. Check it by hand.

Inventory.overCap: {actor} is over the {category} limit ({held}/{limit}). Allowed - a GM granted it.
Inventory.full: You already carry the most {category} you can ({limit}).
Inventory.notCarried: (not picked up - that category is full)

Remnant.reinforced: That Remnant is reinforced and cannot be removed.
Remnant.foundTitle: A trace was copied, and nobody has said what it is
Remnant.faintKept: A Faint Remnant is always Faint, so its Faint box was ticked again. To untick it, give the trace another kind.

deathTied.one: The victim is dead: {n} trace from this chapter nobody had decided about is now marked as tied to the murder. Set the laundry to “Not tied” in the Investigation Dashboard. The students' copies learn the tie when the body is found.
deathTied.other: The victim is dead: {n} traces from this chapter nobody had decided about are now marked as tied to the murder. Set the laundry to “Not tied” in the Investigation Dashboard. The students' copies learn the tie when the body is found.

Remnant.noToken: {actor} has no token on any scene, so the trace could not be left. Tell the GM.
Remnant.noTokenGm: {actor} performed “{action}” with no token anywhere, so no Remnant was placed. Place one by hand if it matters.
Remnant.revealWarning: Remnants are your notes. Revealing this puts it on the map for everyone.
Remnant.searchNote: {actor} searched {room} for a {category} (rolled {total}) and came away with {item} - Tier {tier}.
Remnant.sabotageWorked: It worked: the project is frozen until {repair} is finished.
Remnant.sabotageFailed: It failed - the project is untouched, but the attempt left a trace.
Remnant.projectNote: {actor} worked on {project} in {room}, gaining {progress} progress, and rolled {total} to cover their tracks.
Remnant.projectNoteUncovered: {actor} worked on {project} in {room}, gaining {progress} progress, and did not cover their tracks.
Remnant.cardPlayer: Something here is out of place. What it means is not obvious from looking - Observe the room to work it out.
Remnant.cardUnanalyzed: You have not worked out what this is yet. Analyze it to find out.
Remnant.cardUnread: Not analysed yet. Analyze it to read the rest.

keptOnTokens.one: {n} trace keeps flags of its answer key on its token, which every browser holds: the migration had no row to carry them into, or a later correction stood against them. game.drpg.migrateRemnants() in the console names it.
keptOnTokens.other: {n} traces keep flags of their answer keys on their tokens, which every browser holds: the migration had no row to carry them into, or a later correction stood against them. game.drpg.migrateRemnants() in the console names each.

Remnant.cardEditNote: Saved when you leave the field, and copied onto the token and every Truth Bullet taken from this trace.
Remnant.cardSaveFailed: That did not save. See the console.

report.heading: Remnants
report.reinforcedNote: ★ = reinforced, and the killer cannot remove it.

Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDay: You have already taken a {kind} this time of day.
Rest.alreadyThisSession: You have already taken a {kind} this session.
Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDayShort: already taken this time of day
Rest.wrongRoom: No {kind} in {room}. Rooms that allow it: {rooms}
Rest.noRooms: No room on this map is marked for a {kind} yet. The GM sets that up per scene.
Rest.noKnownRooms: No room you know of allows it.
Rest.manageIntro: Mark which rooms allow a Short Rest and which allow a Long Rest. Per scene, so every season's map can differ.
Rest.noRegions: This scene has no room regions. Draw them on the Regions layer first.

Calls.resolveNext: Your next roll will ask you which statistic to use.
Calls.waitingGm: Waiting on the GM: {call}. The Hope is charged only if they say yes.
Calls.approveCost: {cost} Hope, charged only on a yes.
Calls.send: Ask the GM - {cost} Hope on a yes
Calls.tellGm: Tell the GM what you are about to do with it

tellGmPlaceholder.experience: Which experience, and how it applies to what you are attempting.
tellGmPlaceholder.ultimate: How your talent applies to what you are attempting.

Calls.waitsForGm: The GM has to agree before this is spent. Your Hope is not touched until they do.
Calls.needNote: Write what you are going to do with it first - the GM is being asked to rule on that, not on the Call.
Calls.approveHint: The question is the handbook's: does it GENUINELY apply here? Refusing costs the player nothing.
Calls.refused: {call}: the GM said not this time. Nothing was spent.

sprinted.one: {n} extra crossing this time of day, free of charge.
sprinted.other: {n} extra crossings this time of day, free of charge.

burst.one: Your next action is free - {n} banked.
burst.other: Your next actions are free - {n} banked.

Calls.noPool: This Monokuma has no Despair pool. Check the Despair bar.
Calls.nobodyHere: Nobody else is in this room.
Calls.noItems: Nobody carries anything that can be destroyed.
Calls.armed: {name} may now use {what} on their next roll.
Calls.alreadyArmed: {name} is already holding {call} for their next roll. A second one would add nothing.
Calls.nothingToMark: {name} has nothing left to mark there.
Calls.sealed: {room} is sealed for this time of day.
Calls.effectFailed: {call} was paid for, but its effect could not be applied. Tell the GM.
Calls.refunded: {call} did nothing, so the {cost} it cost has been returned.
Calls.silenced: {name} cannot spend Hope Calls until this time of day ends.
Calls.silencedNotice: Monokuma has silenced you. No Hope Calls until this time of day ends.
Calls.chained: {name} is chained to {room} until this time of day ends.
Calls.chainedNotice: Monokuma chained you here. You cannot leave until this time of day ends.
Calls.chainedBlocked: You are chained here until this time of day ends.
Calls.sealedBlocked: {room} is sealed for this time of day. Nobody gets in.
Calls.freeCritUsed: {name} takes the action with one die already set to 12 and throws the other.

grants.critical: a loaded die (one die set to 12)

Calls.pendingTooltip: Waiting on your next roll: {what}. Spent the moment you roll.
Calls.noExperiences: This character has no experiences written down, so this Call has nothing to add.
Calls.armedTitle: A Call was made for you
Calls.waitsNextRoll: Armed after this window opened: {what}. It is not part of this roll - it waits for your next one.
Calls.armedForYou: Another student spent Hope on you: your next roll has {what}. It applies by itself.
Calls.armedByMonokuma: Monokuma has {what} on your next roll. It applies by itself.
Calls.armedByNobody: Your next roll carries {what}. It applies by itself.
Calls.newRulePrompt: Write the new rule. Every player sees it in chat, word for word.
Calls.newRulePlaceholder: e.g. From now on, nobody may enter the library alone.
Calls.newRuleNote: {cost} Despair buys a permanent change to the game. Make it count.
Calls.newRuleAnnounced: The new rule was announced to everyone.
Calls.noSuchRoom: There is no region called “{room}” on this scene.
Calls.gatherNoRoom: There is no room called “{room}” on {scene}. Nothing was spent.
Calls.progressRefused: {name} could not take the progress - it is already complete.
Calls.cannotAfford: You do not hold enough for this one.

motiveSet.one: The motive is announced. One time of day on the clock.
motiveSet.other: The motive is announced. {n} times of day on the clock.

Calls.gatherRoomGone: The assembly could not be held: "{room}" is not a room on that scene any more. The order has been cleared - the Despair it cost is not coming back, and the cast will have to be moved by hand.
Calls.gatherBody: Everyone to {room}, at the start of the next time of day.
Calls.gatherNote: You have until then. Where you are when it starts is up to you.
Calls.gatherCalled: Everyone is called to {room} for the next time of day.
Calls.gatherCancelled: The assembly in {room} is called off.
Calls.gatherNoRefund: No Despair comes back - the announcement has already been heard.
Calls.notArmedNotCharged: {call} was not armed, and no Hope was taken.
Calls.despairGmOnly: Despair Calls are a Monokuma's to spend, and a Monokuma is a GM.

Monokuma.marked: {name} is now a Monokuma: no actions, no Hope, Despair Calls instead, and free movement.
Monokuma.panelIntro: Tick the actors that are Monokumas, then say whose Despair pool each draws on. Without this, two Monokumas share the pool of whichever GM is looking at the sheet.
Monokuma.panelNote: A Monokuma has no actions and no Hope: their sheet shows Despair Calls instead. The pool decides which GM pays for them.
Monokuma.sharedPool: {name}'s pool is shared by: {actors}. Each Monokuma should have their own.

Overflow.hopeBlocked: The darkening blocks Hope this time of day - nothing was spent.
Overflow.title: Despair overflow
Overflow.caption: Despair overflow
Overflow.clearAsk: Set the spilled Despair back to 0? It holds {count} of {max} now. A darkening already drawn stays until its time of day ends.
Overflow.cleared: The Despair overflow is back to 0.
Overflow.cardBody: {n} points of spilled Despair have found a use. For one time of day, this is what the school becomes:
Overflow.cardBodyTrial: {n} points of spilled Despair have found a use. From the next time of day after the trial, for one time of day, this is what the school becomes:
Overflow.cardLeft: The overflow keeps what it did not spend.
Overflow.armed: Armed for the next time of day · {name}
Overflow.waiting: Waiting for the next time of day · {name}
Overflow.playerHint: Despair that no Monokuma could hold. At {max} the school gets worse for one time of day. How close it is now is the GMs' to know.
Overflow.gmHint: Spilled Despair: {count} of {max}. It fires the moment it reaches {max}: a darkening takes the next time of day, a one-off happens at once.
Overflow.gmHintQueued: Spilled Despair: {count} of {max}. {what} is already drawn for the next time of day, and the counter waits until that time of day has passed.
Overflow.gmHintActive: This time of day is darkened. {count} of {max} spilled Despair has collected since.
Overflow.gmHintActiveFull: This time of day is darkened. {count} of {max} spilled Despair is waiting, and fires when this time of day ends.
Overflow.setupIntro: Despair that will not fit in a full pool stops evaporating and collects here instead. When it reaches the threshold it pays that much, keeps the rest, and ONE thing is drawn from the pool below - never more than one.
Overflow.thresholdHint: Any value from {min} to {max}: the table decides.
Overflow.suggestNone: A suggestion appears here once the season has living students.
Overflow.floorNote: None of these ever goes below one. A time of day with no actions, or a room with no search tokens, is not a harder game - it is a player with nothing to do until the clock moves.
Overflow.currentDrawn: Right now: {count} of {max}. This time of day is under {what}.
Overflow.currentWaiting: Right now: {count} of {max}. {what} was announced in the trial and waits for the next time of day.
Overflow.poolHint: One of these is drawn at random each time the overflow fires - never more than one. Untick anything you do not want in the hat.
Overflow.oneOffHint: These happen once, the moment the overflow fires, instead of lasting the time of day.
Overflow.emptyPool: Nothing is ticked, so the overflow will never fire and never spend the counter. That is a real setting - the counter as pure atmosphere - but nothing will happen until you tick something.
Overflow.silenced: Silence. Nobody is spending Hope Calls this time of day.
Overflow.noHopeNow: Despair. No Hope is earned this time of day.

what.darkness: The lights go further down: {n} fewer crossings in the Eclipse, and an Eclipse that would have let you start anywhere is pulled back to two rooms.
what.shift: Things are not where they were: {n} fewer search tokens in every room.
what.panic: Nobody gets as much done: {n} fewer actions each, on top of anything Wounded already took.
what.despair: No Hope is earned at all. Spending what you already hold still works.
what.silence: No Hope Calls. Not one, by anybody.
what.fog: You cannot find your way for free: no Free Move. Crossings still cost actions as usual.
what.rot: Everything the school owns gets worse at once: {n} durability off every item with more than one point left. Nothing breaks.
what.earthquake: The building shakes and work is undone: every project still under way loses {n} progress.

Overflow.rulesChanged: The overflow has been retuned. It now fires at {n}.
Overflow.explainEmpty: Nothing is in the GM's hat right now, so the overflow will not fire until they put something in it.
Overflow.explainBody: A Monokuma's pool holds {max}. Despair earned past that collects here, in one counter shared by every Monokuma. At the threshold it pays that much, keeps the rest, and draws ONE effect at random from the GM's hat, for one time of day. Feed the Overflow pours Despair in on purpose. A Class Trial verdict empties it; a darkening announced during the trial still comes, at the next time of day.

explainHat.one: One effect is in the hat now.
explainHat.other: {n} effects are in the hat now.

Overflow.explainVeil: Players see “?” rather than the number: when it fires is Monokuma's to know. Nothing about the investigation lives in it.

Eclipse.bodyFirst: A body has been found - start the Investigation first.
Eclipse.incidentFirst: An incident is running - close it first.
Eclipse.trialFirst: A Class Trial is running, so no Eclipse was started: in the trial everybody is in one voice room. End the trial first.

announce.one: Lights out. Place your token - one connected room, no more. Nobody sees anyone else until the Eclipse ends.
announce.other: Lights out. Place your token - up to {n} connected rooms. Nobody sees anyone else until the Eclipse ends.

yourMoves.one: One room crossing. You are in {room}. Drag your token - doors and gaps still apply.
yourMoves.other: {n} room crossings. You are in {room}. Drag your token - doors and gaps still apply.

Eclipse.noMovesLeft: Your Eclipse crossings are used up. Your token has been put back.
Eclipse.actionsLocked: Placement only. Actions are already back; nothing spends them but a Direct Murder until the lights come up.
Eclipse.endPrompt: End the Eclipse and begin the next time of day? Everyone has placed as follows:
Eclipse.announceFree: Lights out. Pick any room on the map and put your token there. Nobody sees anyone else until the Eclipse ends.
Eclipse.yourMovesFree: Any room on the map. You are in {room}. Drag your token wherever you want to start.
Eclipse.murderOnlyInEclipse: Only during an Eclipse. The lights are out and everyone is crossing the map - that is the one moment you can be alone with somebody.
Eclipse.actionsMurderOnly: Placement is running. The only thing an action buys right now is a Direct Murder.
Eclipse.placementOnly: Placement only. Nothing spends an action until the lights come up.
Eclipse.callsLocked: Locked while the Eclipse runs. Every Call unlocks with the next time of day - this is not about what you hold.
Eclipse.murderWindowLocked: The Eclipse is a placement window - nobody has finished moving yet. Open the incident once the lights come up; a trap's card waits on the thread until you do.
Eclipse.murderLocked: The Eclipse is a placement window - nobody has finished moving yet. A Direct Murder declared now waits for the Eclipse to end on its own.
Eclipse.bodyLocked: The Eclipse is running. A body cannot be discovered - by hand or automatically - until everyone has finished placing.
Eclipse.panelLocked: Locked while the Eclipse runs - nobody has finished placing yet.

Movement.unlawfulArrival: {name} reached {room} by a crossing the rules refuse. Until they stand somewhere they could have walked to from {from}, they are no witness to a body and no third party to a murder. Nothing was put back: a GM's move makes the spot they stand on lawful.
Movement.wallCrossed: {name}'s token was moved through a wall on {scene} and was sent back where it stood.
Movement.floorJumped: {name}'s token was moved to another floor on {scene} where no stairs lead, and was sent back where it stood.
Movement.ruleSentBack: {name}'s token was moved into {room} on {scene}, where the rules do not let {name} go, and was put back where {name} last stood.
Movement.dropRemoved: A player placed a token of {name} in {room} on {scene}, where the rules do not let {name} stand. The token was removed.
Movement.droppedFromNowhere: A player placed a token of {name} in {room} on {scene}, where {name} had stood nowhere before. It was judged as an arrival from outside the rooms, so no rule about which rooms connect applied, and it counts as a witness there. Move the token if it should not be there.

Move.title: Move
Move.freeAvailable: Your Free Move for this time of day is still there.
Move.freeSpent: Free Move used - the next room costs an action. You have {left}.
Move.wasFree: That was your Free Move for this time of day.
Move.noBudget: No Free Move and no actions left.
Move.notConnected: {to} is not connected to {from}. From here you can reach: {rooms}
Move.noBudgetLong: No Free Move and no actions left - this crossing was not paid for, so your token was put back.
Move.refundedBack: The GM gave back your last crossing: your token stands where it was before it.
Move.refundedStays: The GM gave back your last crossing, but your token could not be stood where it was before it - ask the GM.
Move.refundedPrice: What the crossing cost is yours again.
Move.refundedNoPrice: The GMs saw nothing it cost, so nothing else came back - ask the GM if it cost you something.
Move.noStairs: No stairs lead from {from} to that floor.
Move.dead: They are dead. The body stays where it fell.

Project.passageRefused: That stretch does not stand between the builder's room and the room beyond: pick it again.
Project.passageNoWall: The builder's room shares no wall with another room on this floor: a secret passage has nowhere to go.
Project.passageNeedsPick: Pick the stretch of wall the secret passage goes through first.
Project.passagePick: Pick the stretch on the wall
Project.passageFrom: From the {room}, where the builder stands.
Project.passageNote: A secret passage through a wall of the room you are in: Hand, Complex (6), always secret. Only you, and whoever the project is shared with before it is finished, will know it.
Project.breachNote: A breach through a wall of the room you are in: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the hole is there for everyone to see.
Project.sealNote: Seal the passage: Hand, Complex (6). Once it is finished the passage is closed, for you and for everyone who knows it; a GM can open it again.
Project.unbreachNote: Close the breach: Body, Complex (6). Once it is finished the wall stands whole again.
Project.repairNote: Repair an item: Hand; Trivial (3) for an item of Tier 0 or 1, Complex (6) for Tier 2 or 3. Once it is finished the item is whole again.
Project.notRepaired: {name} is finished, but its item could not be repaired: {why}
Project.needsKiller: An indirect murder needs a killer: pick who it is visible to, or approve it from the proposal card.
Project.needsKillerNamed: “{name}” cannot become an indirect murder from here - open it and name who the trap belongs to.
Project.title: Project
Project.choosePrompt: Start something new, or push a project that already exists?
Project.agreedWarning: Fill this in as your side of the agreement. The GM reads it, may change the scale, the room or the wording, and only then does the project exist.
Project.startNote: Nothing is created yet. This goes to the GM as a proposal - they approve it, adjust it, or turn it down.
Project.indirectMine: Indirect murder - kept secret, so only you and the GMs see it
Project.traitRequired: A project needs a statistic: pick the one its work demands.
Project.repaired: repaired. {name} can be worked on again.
Project.doneBody: {name} is complete - all {target} progress is in. Ask the GM what it does for you now.
Project.frozenNow: {name} is broken and frozen until {repair} is finished.
Project.alreadyFrozen: {name} is already broken and waiting on a repair.
Project.sabotageNotApplied: The roll succeeded, but no GM confirmed the damage in time. Tell your GM: {name} may not actually be broken.
Project.none: No projects yet. Start one first.
Project.noneToMove: No project here has progress that can move. Finished ones are done, and a sabotaged one waits for its repair.
Project.aloneBonus: Nobody else is in the room, so the project gains +1 progress.
Project.concealSeen: {actor} is busy with something in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.
Project.tracesUncovered: not rolled: the traces stay as they were left.
Project.toolRelief: {item} is Tier {tier}, so every threshold on this roll comes down by {tier}.
Project.roomOnNoScene: No project was made: {room} is a room on no scene now. Name a room a scene holds, or none.
Project.cardFrozen: Broken, and frozen until it is repaired
Project.cardSecret: Secret - only the people ticked on it
Project.cardPublic: Public - anyone who has stood in its room
Project.cardShared: Every project token is a copy of this actor. Open a project from its token on the map.
Project.cardUnknown: You do not know what this is.
Project.createNote: Progress moves only when somebody uses Work on Project - never from attacks or rests. An indirect murder is made secret automatically.
Project.name: Name
Project.visibleToNote: Ticked players see the project while it is secret. Whoever is building it always sees it, ticked or not.
Project.manageTooltip: Set which room each project belongs to, and who may see it

Project.secretNote: Indirect murder projects are secret by default: only the killer and the GMs see them. Share to bring in a co-conspirator.
Project.changeImage: Click to change this project's image
Project.tokenMoved: {project} now belongs to {to} - its token was moved there from {from}.

sweptOld.one: {n} project token was left on the map by a project that no longer exists, and has been removed.
sweptOld.other: {n} project tokens were left on the map by projects that no longer exist, and have been removed.

Project.glyphNote: Under the Stained Glass theme the Projects tray draws this instead of the image, in the interface's colour. The image is used everywhere else.
Project.deleteNote: Tick Delete and Save to remove a project for good. Its progress and metadata do not come back.
Project.shareIntro: Let another player see this project. Players can bring in a co-conspirator; GMs can share with anyone.
Project.noPlayers: There are no players to share with.
Project.alreadyFull: {name} is already at {current}/{target}. No progress left to add.
Project.alreadyEmpty: {name} is already at 0. Nothing left to take away.
Project.noneHere: There is no project started in {room}.
Project.allSabotaged: Everything here is already broken or is itself a repair: {names}.
Project.someSabotaged: Not offered - already broken, or a repair project: {names}.
Project.editProgressNote: Progress is kept: this project is at {current}/{target}. Lowering the scale below what is earned clamps it.
Project.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}”? Its progress goes with it.
Project.conditionPlaceholder: whoever opens the dumbwaiter after dark
Project.conditionNote: Indirect murder only. Name a condition instead of a victim - whoever meets it is who the trap catches.
Project.trapNoCondition: No condition was written down for this trap. Agree one before firing it.
Project.proposalPrompt: Say what you are actually doing and why here. The GM reads this with your answers and decides - they may change the scale, the room or the wording before it starts.
Project.proposalPlaceholder: What you are building, and what you want out of it…
Project.proposerKnows: Your project “{name}” is under way in {room}. It shows on your Projects tray and on the map.

RollDialog.modeLocked: Who sees this roll is set by the game, not here.
RollDialog.modeRoom: The GMs, you and the room

RollDialog.reactionLocked: A statistic rolled on its own is a reaction: it costs nothing and earns nothing. Hope and Despair come from actions.
RollDialog.unlockedByCall: Unlocked by a Call you paid for.

RollDialog.mixedAdvantage: Advantage - {sources}. Together that is one bonus die. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.mixedDisadvantage: Disadvantage - {sources}. Together that is one penalty die. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.advantageCapped: More than {cap} dice stops being a roll, so it stops at {cap}.

Tables.whereNote: The tables live in the Rollable Tables sidebar, in the “Danganronpa RPG” folder. A Search in a room draws from that room's own tables first, then from the tier pools, then from the module's built-in lists.
Tables.noTierPools: No tier pools yet. Install them with “Install / reinstall” below.
Tables.noRoomPools: No room pools yet. Name one below.
Tables.newTierPoolNote: A tier pool is named for its category and its tier, as “DRPG Tools - Tier 2” is. Usually you do not make one by hand: “Install / reinstall” below builds them all.
Tables.newTierPoolForms: “{name}” is not a tier pool. Name it for a category and a tier, one of: {forms} - where N is a tier from {low} to {high}.
Tables.renameOtherPool: “{name}” would name another pool. This one holds the items of “{pool}”: keep its category and tier in the name.
Tables.installTabNote: “Install / reinstall” below builds the default set - one table per category and tier. If they already exist, you choose between keeping yours and rebuilding.
Tables.editorIntro: Everything a Search can turn up. Pick a table on the left to see what is in it; the form below adds one item to as many tables as you tick.
Tables.roomBreakdown: Sorted by what the tier pools say each name is. A flat room table still answers whatever category a Search asks for - name a table "Room - Murder Weapons" to have that decided here instead.
Tables.unfiledNote: No tier pool holds these names, so the module cannot say what they are or how good they are. In a flat room table they can come up for any category. Use the arrows on a row to put one in a tier pool.
Tables.placeIntro: Tick every pool this item should be in. Ticking a new one copies it there, unticking one takes it out, and unticking the pool you are looking at moves it.
Tables.placeRolesNote: The description, the picture and the roles travel with it. A tier pool below Tier 2 takes no roles, and no pool takes a role that is its own category.
Tables.placeNone: An item has to live in at least one pool. Use the row's ✕ to delete it outright.
Tables.placeUnchanged: {name} is already in exactly those pools.
Tables.noneYet: No item tables yet - create the default set below.
Tables.tierTargetIs: Goes into {table}. Worked out from the category and tier above.
Tables.tierTargetNone: No tier pool exists for that category and tier - it will only live in the rooms you tick below. Install the pools from the Tier pools tab.
Tables.roomTargets: Room tables it also appears in:
Tables.noRoomTables: No room tables yet - create one on the Room pools tab.
Tables.rolesTierOnly: Two jobs start at tier {tier} - an item this cheap does one.
Tables.rolesNote: Also works as - tick anything this entry can do besides its own category. A screwdriver under Tools that is also a Murder Weapon gives advantage on an attack as well as on project work, and still takes one slot.
Tables.addNote: The icon and the description travel with it: whoever finds this item gets both on their sheet.
Tables.needsTable: Pick a tier table or tick at least one room table.
Tables.newPoolNote: A room table is what a room stocks - point a room at it in Room Setup's “Draws from”. Tier tables answer dice rolls and cannot be assigned to rooms. A room's own tables answer a Search there before the tier pools do, and one named “«Room» - Tier N” answers that roll first.
Tables.newPoolTierName: That name matches the tier-table pattern (“DRPG … - Tier N”) - a room table needs its own name.
Tables.presetRoomNoTable: {room} draws from no table of its own. Point it at one in Room Setup to keep finds like this there.
Tables.presetRoomTier: {room} has no table for this tier yet: make “{name}” on the Room pools tab to keep finds of this tier there.
Tables.tierPoolCreated: "{name}" is ready, and the module recognised it: items in it are filed by its category and tier, so a usable drawn from it knows what it does.
Tables.poolCreated: Room table “{name}” created. Point a room at it in Room Setup.
Tables.renameNote: A tier pool keeps a name of its category and tier. A room table can take any other name.
Tables.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}” and the {n} entries in it? This cannot be undone.

GiveBack.menuHint: What this module changes in Foundry and Daggerheart, and the button that puts it back. Press it before you switch the module off.
GiveBack.title: Give back Foundry's settings
GiveBack.intro: While it runs, this module changes these settings of Foundry, Daggerheart and the modules it needs:

what.automation: Daggerheart's Vulnerable and Defeated automations are off: Breakdown and Wounded take their place.
what.playerFiles: Players and Trusted Players cannot browse or upload files ('Keep players out of the file browser').
what.isoWelcome: Isometric Perspective's welcome window stays closed for everyone.
what.dhWelcome: Daggerheart's welcome journal does not open for anyone.
what.liveKitInFoundry: LiveKit's voice stays inside the Foundry window for everyone.
what.rtcDock: Foundry's camera dock is folded while the voice tile is on, and no camera pops out.
what.sceneVision: On scenes with rooms, the rooms take over Foundry's own vision, fog and global light: turning 'Rooms decide what players can see' off gives them back.
what.diceLook: While 'One dice look for the table' is on, every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice in one full Gamemaster's look. Give back does not change this, and nobody's own earlier look comes back: the module never kept it.

GiveBack.givenBackState: Given back: the module leaves these settings alone until you hold them again.
GiveBack.filesStay: Give back leaves the file permissions as they are now: if players should browse or upload files, grant it in Foundry's permissions.
GiveBack.beforeOff: Before you switch the module off, press Give them back here and turn 'Rooms decide what players can see' off.
GiveBack.heldAgain: The module holds its settings again.
GiveBack.automationOff: Daggerheart's Vulnerable and Defeated automations are switched off: Breakdown and Wounded take their place. To have them back, press Give back Foundry's settings in this module's settings.
GiveBack.automationUnknown: The values Daggerheart's Vulnerable and Defeated automations had before this module are not known: it switched them off before it kept anything. Give them back sets Daggerheart's defaults - both on. If this world had them off, switch them off again in Daggerheart's settings.
GiveBack.fullGmOnly: Only a full Gamemaster can give these back: Foundry lets only a full Gamemaster change the file permissions.
GiveBack.partly: Given back, except: {parts}. Its value is still kept - open this window again and press Give them back.
GiveBack.failed: Foundry's settings could not be given back or held. The console says why.
GiveBack.preSeason: Foundry's settings are given back: the module holds none of them - Daggerheart's automations, the file permissions, the players' held settings. To hold them again, open Give back Foundry's settings (Set the season up, or this module's settings) and press Hold them again.

Frisk.interrupted: The moment has passed: this cannot be done now.

Reroll.searchNeverRan: The room was never searched - the search token was refused - so there is nothing to draw again.
Reroll.searchStashStands: The stash find stands: new dice do not open the stash twice.

Reroll.title: Reroll
Reroll.nothingToReroll: You have not rolled anything, so there is nothing to take back.
Reroll.notARoll: Your last message carries no dice.
Reroll.failed: The reroll could not be applied. Tell the GM.
Reroll.despairGained: The new result is a Despair result: {name} gains 1 Despair.
Reroll.despairReturned: The old result was a Despair result: 1 Despair is returned to {name}.
Reroll.critHopeGained: The new result is a critical: you gain the second point of Hope a crit is worth.
Reroll.critHopeReturned: The old result was a critical: the second point of Hope it paid is taken back.
Reroll.progressAdjusted: {name}: progress from this action changed from {was} to {now}.
Reroll.noReplay: Nothing but the dice to take back: this roll left no lasting effect.
Reroll.replayFailed: The dice were rerolled, but the action could not be replayed. Tell the GM what the first roll had already done.
Reroll.observeReplayed: The same trace goes back to the GM with the new roll. They will say what you find this time.
Reroll.analyzeReplayed: The same Truth Bullet is analyzed again with the new roll. Any lock the first attempt left is lifted first.
Reroll.crisisReplayed: The crisis action is taken back and made again with the new roll - the damage, the trace and any hindrance go with it. The turn is not spent twice.
Reroll.deathStands: A crisis action that killed cannot be taken back: the death stands.
Reroll.busy: A Reroll of this character is already being made. Wait for it to finish.
Reroll.messageGone: The roll is no longer in the chat, so there is nothing to throw again. Nothing was spent.
Reroll.interrupted: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload before its new dice counted. The first roll stands, and the Hope paid for it is given back.
Reroll.interruptedGm: {name}'s Reroll ({action}) was cut short by a reload while its action was being taken back and made again. The first roll was {first}, the new one {total}; the card shows the new one. What the first roll did may be undone only in part: check by hand what this action leaves - progress, items, traces, damage, a turn - and settle it. The Hope stays paid, and this roll cannot be rerolled again.
Reroll.interruptedPending: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload while it was being made. The GM will settle it; the Hope stays paid.
Reroll.interruptedPaying: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload while its {cost} Hope was being paid, before the dice were thrown again. The first roll stands and can still be rerolled. Check {name}'s Hope by hand: the payment may or may not have been written.
Reroll.interruptedGivingBack: {name}'s Reroll did not stand, and a reload cut short the giving back of its {cost} Hope. The first roll is back on the card and can still be rerolled. Check {name}'s Hope by hand: it may or may not have come back.
Reroll.interruptedHope: {name}'s Reroll was cut short by a reload. The first roll stands; the GM will check the Hope.

Reroll.observeBusy: The GM is still describing what this Observe found. Reroll it once the result is in. Nothing was spent.
Reroll.diceChanged: This roll's dice are not the ones the GMs kept: a change to them is being put back. Reroll it in a moment. Nothing was spent.
Reroll.trailStands: The dice are rewritten, but what you planted is already lying in the room - a reroll cannot pick it back up. Ask the GM if it should come out.
Reroll.authorsCopyBack: The new dice take back the Truth Bullet of the trace you left.
Reroll.stealStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. Your hand has already been in their pocket, and putting something back is something they would watch you do.
Reroll.friskStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. The whole room saw how it went.
Reroll.rummageStands: The dice are rewritten, but the moment is not. They already know whether you got a proper look.
Reroll.rummageSeen: The dice are rewritten, but what you saw stays seen.
Reroll.rummageLate: The moment has passed: {who} is no longer within reach.

Season.roomGuide: Walls first, then a Region for each room, drawn to them with snapping on; a room may be drawn as several regions of one name. A region is a room only once a GM ticks “This is a room” for it in Room Setup (the Doors tab): a region nobody ticked, a passage (a region that teleports a token or changes its level) and a region a player drew are no rooms and never count as neighbours. phase.eclipse: The lights are out. Everyone places their token - up to two connected rooms, or anywhere at night - and nobody can see who went where. Your actions are already refilled, but nothing spends them except a Direct Murder, and nobody makes a Call until the lights come up. It is the game's one moment of total cover, and it is where a murder usually starts.
phase.dailyLife: Ordinary days inside the school. You have two actions each time of day to search rooms, work on projects, rest, talk, and prepare. Nobody has died yet this chapter - this is the part where you decide who you trust.
phase.investigation: A body has been found. Observe traces on the map, Analyze what you collect, and every Truth Bullet you build is one you can present at the trial. What you fail to find, you will not have.
phase.classTrial: Everyone is in the room and one of you did it. Testimony, Objections, and finally the vote. Get it right and the killer is punished; get it wrong and everybody else is.

despair.title: What Despair is
despair.what: Despair is the GM side's currency. It fills when rolls at the table come up with Despair rather than Hope - which is to say, it is fed by your bad luck and your risks.
despair.spent: It is spent on Despair Calls: the moves that make life harder - pushing a scene, hardening a room, turning a screw. The more of it there is, the more the school can do to you.
despair.masked: Every pool's count is public - the rows show how full each one is. Only the overflow's count is hidden from you.

status.actionsWhat: Two each time of day. Searching a room, working on a project, observing a trace, analyzing a Truth Bullet - each of those is one. A Short Rest costs one, a Long Rest both.
status.actionsWounded: With all your Health marked you get one instead of two, until somebody patches you up.
status.actionsNow: You have {left} of {max} left this time of day.
status.moveWhat: One move between rooms each time of day that costs you nothing. After that, changing rooms costs an action like anything else.
status.moveSpent: Your Free Move is gone this time of day - moving now costs an action.
status.hopeWhat: Hope is yours, and it is spent on Hope Calls: helping somebody else's roll, leaning on an Experience, invoking your Ultimate, rerolling. It comes back when rolls go your way.
status.monokumaActions: You have no action economy. A Monokuma is skipped when actions are refilled, and spends none.
status.monokumaMove: Movement costs you nothing and grants you nothing - there is no Free Move to keep track of.
status.monokumaDespair: You spend Despair where a student spends Hope. The pools are at the top of the screen.
status.monokumaWalls: Walls and locked doors do not apply to you.

projects.title: What a project is
projects.what: A project is something that takes longer than one action: building it, fixing it, poisoning it, digging through it. Each one lives in a room and only moves when somebody works on it there.
projects.progress: Working on a project is an action, and a roll - how well it goes decides how much progress it takes. When the bar fills, the thing is done.
projects.secret: Some projects are private to the people working on them. If you cannot see one, it is not on your list.

overlap.title: Rooms overlap
overlap.fact: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms.
overlap.deep: About {squares} squares of floor belong to both rooms, reaching {depth} squares in.
overlap.why: Where two rooms overlap, one room's border runs across the other's floor with no wall near it, and the whole shared border reads as one doorway. Rooms should touch; a sliver thinner than a quarter square is ignored.

adrift.fact: {squares} squares of border with no wall.
adrift.why: A border drawn away from the wall it stands for turns that whole side of the room into a doorway: the wall is never found, so nothing closes it.

sealed.title: No way out: walled all round
sealed.fact: Every stretch of the border is walled.
sealed.why: Nothing glows as a doorway. If the room is sealed on purpose, leave it; if not, the door is missing.

isolated.title: No way out: no room beside it
isolated.fact: No room within a square of the border.
isolated.why: The next room is more than a square away, so the two never meet at a doorway. Rooms should touch along the edge they share.

lattice.problem: Corners off the map's own lattice
lattice.why: The rest of the map is drawn to a half-square lattice. Draw with snapping on: a corner a fraction of a square out cannot be seen by eye and is enough to make two rooms overlap or miss.

Relay.refused: Refused a Daggerheart change from {name}: {what}. Nothing was changed.
Relay.forged: {name} sent a change Daggerheart does not make for a player: {what}. Nothing was changed. If nobody at the table did anything unusual, tell the module's author - it may be a Daggerheart feature this module has not met yet.
Relay.unguarded: The guard on Daggerheart's GM relay could not be put in place on Daggerheart {version}. This session, changes a player's Daggerheart asks your browser to make are NOT checked. Tell the module's author.
